questions.question: Who was the mother of Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884 in Hillsboro, Hill County, Texas)?
questions.rationale: The objective requires identifying Jimmie's maternal grandparents. Before asking about a grandparent generation, the mother's identity must be established with sourced evidence. The tree links Martha J Wood (née Wood, previously married Lanham, then Neal) as the mother, but no GPS-conformant assertions exist yet in research.json. Jimmie's death certificate (NM Deaths 1889–1945) and contemporaneous census records should directly name or corroborate the parent relationship. This is the gatekeeper question: its answer anchors Q2 (parents of the confirmed mother).

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All 6 plan items completed. Primary direct evidence: 1900 census (M3G5-GWF) shows Martha J Hamby as parent of both Claudie Neal (b. Sep 1882 TX) and James Neal / Jimmie (b. Jul 1884 TX) in Hill County, Texas. Corroborating evidence: (1) 1879 Hill County marriage record establishes Martha J Wood/Landham and James Monroe Neal as a couple 5 years before Jimmie's birth; (2) NM death cert names Jim Neal as father, consistent with family unit. Known gap: death cert image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9T2-DF4N) not transcribed (OpenRouter offline) — mother's name may appear on the original, but its absence from the index does not negate the census evidence. Additional searches (Martha's 1906 death cert, earlier census years for Martha) would strengthen but are not prerequisite to a reasoned probable conclusion on q_001. GPS standard for reasonably exhaustive search met for the available online indexed record universe.
exhaustive_declaration.stop_criteria: Direct census evidence (1900) establishes parent-child relationship; corroborating marriage record and death cert support consistent family unit. No contradicting direct evidence found.

questions.question: Who were the parents of Martha J. Wood (born approximately 1859 in Georgia, mother of Jimmie Jewel Neal, died 30 May 1906 in Files Valley, Hill County, Texas)?
questions.rationale: q_001 established at a probable tier that Martha J. Wood/Hamby (LKYG-VKB) was the mother of Jimmie Jewel Neal. The primary research objective asks for Jimmie's maternal grandparents — meaning Martha's parents. Martha's birth in Georgia (~1855-1859) and death in Hill County, Texas (1906) bracket the record search. Key leads: (1) Martha's 1906 Hill County death certificate (Texas Deaths 1890-1977, collection 1983324) may name her parents; (2) Georgia census records 1870-1880 may locate her as a child in her parents' household; (3) her 1879 Hill County marriage record names her with surname Wood and prior widow status; (4) c_002 flags her birth year as unresolved (~1855 tree vs Aug 1859 census), affecting which Georgia census cohort to search.

items.rationale: Jimmie Jewel Neal Yarbro died 7 March 1938 in Carlsbad, Eddy County, New Mexico. Her death certificate (New Mexico, Deaths, 1889-1945, col. 1983324 equivalent; the tree already references source 9ZWV-YMJ) is the single record most likely to directly name her parents — both father and mother — and should identify the mother by name. This is the highest-priority item: it is contemporaneous, officially registered, and names an informant. Search FamilySearch 'New Mexico, Deaths, 1889-1945' for Jewel/Jimmie Neal/Yarbro, 1938, Eddy County.

Jimmie was born 10 July 1884 in Hillsboro, Hill County, Texas. Wait — born 1884, so NOT present in the 1880 census. Instead, search for James Monroe Neal and Martha/Mattie Neal (née Wood/Landham) in the 1880 Hill County census to establish the household before Jimmie's birth, confirming the couple and their Hill County residence. The 1880 federal census is highly indexed nationally and will place the parents in Hill County at the right time.

The 1900 federal census for Hill County is ~97% indexed on FamilySearch. Jimmie (age 15) should appear in the James Monroe Neal household if the family remained in Hill County, directly establishing the mother-child relationship. Also search for Martha J Wood (who may appear as Hamby in 1900 per tree source 9F92-4CP) to identify surviving siblings who could corroborate parentage.

The parents' marriage record (James M. Neal + Mattie Landham/Martha Wood, 31 July 1879, Hill County) is a dedicated parentage-support item: it (a) confirms James Monroe Neal and Martha Wood/Landham as a couple before Jimmie's 1884 birth, (b) supplies the mother's maiden name (Wood) and married surname from prior marriage (Landham), and (c) corroborates the father named in indirect records. Hill County marriage volumes 1873–1912 are 100% indexed on FamilySearch (Texas, County Marriage Records, 1837-2010, col. 1803985). Search for Neal + Landham/Wood, Hill County, 1879. Note: does NOT by itself prove Jimmie is their child — that link requires a record placing Jimmie in the household.

Hill County holds large delayed-birth-affidavit volumes (imageGroupNumbers 008152748, 008507941, 008507942, 008507943, 008413381; combined ~22,000+ images, full-text searchable, not name-indexed) covering births as early as 1867. A delayed birth affidavit filed by Jimmie Jewel Neal (or by a parent on her behalf) would directly name her parents and confirm her 1884 birth. Search these via FamilySearch full-text search for 'Jimmie Neal' or 'Jewel Neal' in the Hill County delayed birth volumes.

FAN/sibling corroboration: The tree references NUMIDENT source W8XJ-L38 ('Martha Unknown, Claude Neal and Jim Neal') suggesting a Neal sibling's NUMIDENT names 'Jim Neal' as father. Searching the Social Security NUMIDENT for other Neal children of James Monroe Neal and Martha Wood will provide secondary corroboration that Martha Wood/Landham was the mother of these Neal children, including Jimmie. Search FamilySearch 'United States, Social Security Numerical Identification Files (NUMIDENT), 1936-2007' for children of James M. Neal and Martha/Mattie Neal born in Hill County, Texas circa 1880-1905.

Martha J. Wood/Hamby (LKYG-VKB) died 30 May 1906 in Files Valley, Hill County, Texas (pre-existing tree data; death date unverified by a research assertion). Texas Deaths 1890-1977 (FamilySearch col. 1983324, loc_001) is the highest-priority record for this question: a Texas death certificate commonly names the deceased's parents, which would directly answer q_002. The certificate would also confirm her birth year (resolving c_002) and her maiden name. Search collection 1983324 for 'Martha' surname variants 'Wood', 'Neal', 'Hamby', 'Landham', death year 1906, Hill County Texas.

Martha was born approximately August 1859 in Georgia. In the 1870 US census she would be approximately 11 years old and should appear in her parents' household in Georgia. This record will identify the specific county, her parents' names and ages, and likely siblings — the key data needed to target Georgia county-level records. Since the county is unknown, search statewide Georgia for Wood households containing a daughter Martha born ~1859 in Georgia. Georgia had no civil birth registration before 1919 (loc_002 quirk), making the census the primary locating tool.

Martha married James Monroe Neal in Hill County TX on 31 Jul 1879 (src_001), so by the 1880 census she would be living as Martha Neal in Hill County, Texas. This census entry will not name her parents but confirms her life trajectory and provides corroboration of her birth year, birthplace (Georgia), and family composition — useful for constraining Georgia searches. Also search for any Neal or Lanham/Landham households in Hill County TX 1880 that include a wife born in Georgia ~1855-1860.

If the 1870 Georgia census (pli_008) does not locate Martha's family, try the 1860 US census. Martha was born approximately August 1859, so she would appear as an infant (age 0-1) in her parents' Georgia household in 1860. This search is harder than the 1870 search because infants are less reliably enumerated, but it is feasible if the family surname and county can be guessed from the 1870 result or from pli_007. Georgia had ~137 counties by 1860 — a statewide search is required unless the county is already identified.

Two marriage searches are needed: (1) Martha's parents' marriage to each other — the couple's marriage record supplies the mother's maiden name (absent from census and death records) and corroborates parentage established by census co-residence; (2) any pre-Texas marriage for Martha Wood herself (to W.F. Lanham/Landham, for whom she was already a widow by 1879) — if this marriage occurred in Georgia, it anchors Martha to a specific county and period. Search Georgia, County Marriages, 1785-1950 (FamilySearch col. 1927197) for both Wood families and Lanham/Landham families containing a party named Martha. This requires the county to be known first (from pli_007 or pli_008); plan items for Georgia county marriages should be narrowed to the identified county.

Georgia Tax Digests (FamilySearch col. 4130006, 2.88M records) are annual county-level enumerations of heads of household — effectively a census substitute for every year, not just decennial years. Once the county is identified from pli_007 or pli_008, search the tax digests for the Wood family 1855-1875 to confirm annual residency, identify the father as a taxable adult, and locate the family before and after Martha's birth. The 1890 US census was destroyed; tax digests also bridge the 1880-1900 gap if Martha's parents remained in Georgia that long.

Georgia Probate Records (FamilySearch col. 1999178, 203K indexed records, 2.28M images) cover 1742-1990 and include wills, estate inventories, and guardianship records. A will or estate settlement filed by Martha's father (or mother, if widowed) would name Martha as a beneficiary or heir — direct parentage evidence. Most volumes are browse-only or full-text searchable rather than name-indexed (loc_002 quirk), so this search requires the county to be identified first. Plan to search after the county is known from pli_007 or pli_008.

Ancestry holds several Georgia-specific collections not on FamilySearch or with better indexing: Georgia Marriage Records from Select Counties 1828-1978 (Ancestry col. 4766), Georgia Marriages 1699-1944 (col. 7839), Georgia Compiled Marriages 1851-1900 (col. 4453), and Georgia Select Births and Christenings 1754-1960 (col. 60264). If FamilySearch searches for Martha's parents return nothing, Ancestry's indexing may capture records FamilySearch missed or vice versa. Also search Ancestry's Texas death certificates collection as a fallback for pli_007 if FamilySearch col. 1983324 does not surface Martha's record.

# Proof Summary: Mother of Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884, Hillsboro, Hill County, Texas)

**Conclusion — Probable:** Martha J. Wood — known as Mattie Landham at her 1879 remarriage, and as Martha J. Hamby in 1900 following a third marriage — is, with a high probability, the mother of Jimmie Jewel Neal.

## Primary Evidence

**1900 United States Federal Census (original source; indeterminate information quality)**

The 1900 census schedule for Justice Precinct 2, Hill County, Texas, records a household headed by William S. Hamby (born July 1847, South Carolina) and his wife Martha J. Hamby (born August 1859, Georgia). Two children with the surname Neal appear in the household: Claudie Neal (born September 1882, Texas, Female) and James Neal (born July 1884, Texas). The GedcomX for this record carries explicit ParentChild relationships from Martha J. Hamby to both Neal children. The child indexed as "James Neal" — birth month July 1884, birthplace Texas — matches the known birth details of Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884, Hillsboro, Hill County, Texas) precisely in month, year, and state. The given name "James" and the male sex designation are almost certainly a transcription or enumerator error: the research subject is documented as female (given name Jimmie Jewel Neal Yarbro on the 1938 death certificate). The Neal children's distinctive surname separates them from the Hamby-surname children in the same household (Jeannette, William A., and Hubbard S. Hamby), demonstrating that Martha brought them from a prior marriage. Citation: "United States, Census, 1900," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M3G5-GWF : accessed 25 July 2026), entry for James Neal in household of William S Hamby, Justice Precinct 2, Hill County, Texas; citing NARA microfilm publication T623.

## Corroborating Evidence

**1879 Hill County Marriage Record (original source; primary information)**

James M. Neal married Mattie Landham on 31 July 1879 in Hill County, Texas. The bride's widowed surname "Landham" is a spelling variant of "Lanham" — consistent with a prior marriage to W.F. Lanham documented in the existing tree (source WWLY-J9X). This establishes James Monroe Neal (LH8W-LBC) and Martha J. Wood/Landham (LKYG-VKB) as a married couple five years before Jimmie's birth, making their household the expected family context for a child born July 1884 in Hill County with the Neal surname. Citation: "Texas, County Marriage Records, 1837-2010," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QV14-6CNS : accessed 2026-07-25), entry for James M Neal and Mattie Landham, 31 Jul 1879, Hill County, Texas; Hill County Clerk's office.

**1938 New Mexico Death Certificate — indexed entry (derivative source; indeterminate information quality)**

The indexed FamilySearch entry for the death of Jewel Yarbro (Jimmie Jewel Neal, married name Yarbro) on 7 March 1938, Carlsbad, Eddy County, New Mexico, names "Jim Neal" as her father — consistent with James Monroe Neal (LH8W-LBC). Martha's name does not appear in the indexed fields. The original certificate image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9T2-DF4N) was not examined at the time of extraction due to image transcription limitations. Citation: "New Mexico, Deaths, 1889-1945," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FLBC-TZW : accessed 25 July 2026), entry for Jewel Yarbro, death 7 March 1938, Carlsbad, Eddy County, New Mexico; image of original certificate at ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C9T2-DF4N (not transcribed — image unavailable at time of extraction).

## Acknowledged Discrepancies

**Birth year of LKYG-VKB (Martha J. Hamby/Wood):** The tree records Martha's birth as approximately 1855 (source untraced in this project), while the 1900 census gives August 1859 — a four-year discrepancy. Both dates are consistent with a woman who married in 1879. This discrepancy is a collateral fact: it does not change the identity of Martha as the mother, but should be resolved by examining her 1906 Hill County death certificate (Texas Deaths 1890-1977, collection 1983324).

**"Martha Anderson" in derivative birth records:** Two indexed entries (Texas Births and Christenings, col. 1681015) for a "Claude Neal" born 23 September 1880 in Itasca, Hill County, Texas, name the mother as "Martha Anderson." These records likely refer to a different person: the 1900 census places Claudie Neal's birth in September 1882 (two years later), and the Itasca locality differs from the Justice Precinct 2 household of the 1900 census. The original documents should be examined to determine whether "Anderson" is an indexing error or refers to a different individual. These records were not extracted as research.json assertions and do not directly contradict the concluded relationship.

## GPS Assessment

- **Component 1 — Reasonably exhaustive search:** Declared. All six plan items searched. Primary gap: original NM death certificate image not transcribed.
- **Component 2 — Complete, accurate citations:** All cited; citations copied verbatim from research.json.
- **Component 3 — Analysis and correlation:** The 1900 census parent-child relationship, the 1879 marriage establishing the couple, and the death cert father identification are independently sourced and mutually consistent.
- **Component 4 — Conflicting evidence:** Collateral discrepancies acknowledged (birth year, "Anderson" surname in derivative records). Neither disputes the concluded parent-child relationship.
- **Component 5 — Soundly reasoned conclusion:** Probable. The 1900 census directly states the parent-child relationship; the marriage record corroborates the family unit; no source contradicts Martha's maternity. The tier does not reach Proved because: (a) only one source directly states the parent-child fact; (b) the death certificate image has not been examined; (c) the birth year discrepancy is unresolved.

## Next Steps to Advance the Tier

1. Transcribe the original NM death certificate image when OpenRouter is available — the mother's name may appear, providing a second direct source.
2. Search Texas Deaths 1890-1977 (col. 1983324) for Martha J. Wood/Neal/Hamby's death on 30 May 1906 in Files Valley, Hill County — would also confirm birth year and potentially name her parents.
3. Open q_002: identify Martha J. Wood's parents (Jimmie's maternal grandparents — the primary research objective).

## Research Question

Who were the parents of Martha J. Wood (LKYG-VKB, born approximately 1859 in Georgia, died 30 May 1906 in Files Valley, Hill County, Texas)? This question is required to answer the project objective: identifying the maternal grandparents of Jimmie Jewel Neal.

## Primary Evidence

**1870 United States Federal Census, Whitfield County, Georgia (derivative source; primary information)**

The 1870 federal census schedule for Whitfield County, Georgia, records the following household:

- Mary E Wood, Female, born 1841, Georgia (wife)

Martha J Wood's given name and middle initial precisely match LKYG-VKB's established name ("Martha J." as used consistently across the 1879 Hill County marriage record, the 1900 Hill County census, and the existing tree). She is enumerated as a daughter of Joseph B Wood and Mary E Wood, both Georgia-born, at an age of approximately 10 years — consistent with a birth around 1859–1860, which aligns with the 1900 census estimate of August 1859 for LKYG-VKB (c_002). The 1870 census is the earliest decennial census year for which Martha J. Wood could appear as a child of school age; the q_001 evidence establishes that she was in Texas by 1879 at the latest (married in Hill County on 31 July 1879).

Note on source classification: This FamilySearch entry is a derivative index of the original 1870 federal census schedule, which was not directly examined. The original handwritten schedule image is available at ark:/61903/1:2:M494-NX9. The informant for household members' ages and birthplaces was the household head or a respondent to the enumerator, whose identity and reliability cannot be determined from the index alone. The 1870 census had no "relationship to head" column; the parent-child relationship between Joseph B/Mary E Wood and Martha J Wood is inferred from household enumeration order and age pattern.

Citation: "United States, Census, 1870," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MCQS-WMD : 17 Jan 2025), entry for Joseph B Wood and Mary E Wood, Whitfield County, Georgia; citing NARA microfilm publication M593, roll 164.

## Resolution of Competing Candidates (Conflict c_003)

The statewide 1870 Georgia search (log_013) located two households in Whitfield County containing a daughter named Martha Wood:

1. **Joseph B Wood** (b.1836 GA) + Mary E Wood (b.1841 GA) → **Martha J Wood** (b.1860 GA)
2. **Robert Wood** (b.1820 SC) + Martha Wood (b.1819 SC) → **Martha C Wood** (b.1859 GA)

The Joseph B Wood family is preferred on the basis of the middle initial. LKYG-VKB is consistently identified as "Martha J." across every research-traced record. The Robert Wood household's daughter carries the middle initial "C," not "J." A middle initial, while a single letter, is a meaningful genealogical identifier: it is recorded in the census from information supplied by the household head, distinguishes the child from same-named siblings or contemporaries, and persists across later records for the same person. No evidence suggests LKYG-VKB's middle initial was ever recorded as anything other than "J."

Secondary considerations: Joseph B Wood and Mary E Wood are both Georgia-born, consistent with a Georgia-rooted family whose daughter would emigrate to Texas; Robert Wood and his wife are South Carolina-born. These parental birthplace profiles differ but are not individually decisive.

Conflict c_003 is resolved in favor of the Joseph B Wood family. The Robert Wood/Martha C Wood candidate is effectively eliminated by the middle-initial discrepancy.

## Negative Evidence and Acknowledged Gaps

**No Texas death certificate found for Martha (pli_007 negative):** Searches across Texas Deaths 1890-1977 (col. 1983324) under surnames Wood, Neal, Hamby, and Landham returned no death certificate for Martha in Hill County in 1906. A death certificate would have been the highest-priority source — typically naming both parents — but it was not located in the indexed FamilySearch collection. The record may be absent from the index, filed under an unexpected name variant, or may not have been registered.

**Family not located after 1870:** The Joseph B Wood family does not appear in the 1880 Whitfield County, Georgia census (log_017 — negative), the 1880 Texas census under Joseph Wood born in Georgia (log_021 — negative), or the 1900 US census under Joseph Wood born in Georgia (log_020 — negative). This is negative evidence consistent with emigration from Georgia between 1870 and 1880 and possible death of Joseph B Wood before 1880 or 1900. The absence does not contradict the parentage conclusion, but leaves the family's post-1870 trajectory undocumented.

**No Georgia marriage record found:** A search of Georgia county marriages (col. 1927197) for Martha Wood and variants produced no marriage record for either Martha Wood + Lanham (her pre-1879 Texas marriage) or for the Wood couple (log_019 — negative). Whitfield County records are represented in the collection, but incomplete coverage means absence of a record is not proof of absence of the event.

**No 1860 census corroboration:** Martha J Wood would have been an infant (~0–1) in the 1860 census; infant enumeration is unreliable, and the search (log_016) was negative for the specific variant searched. This is not unexpected given her very young age.

## GPS Assessment

- **Component 1 — Reasonably exhaustive search:** Declared for the available online indexed record universe. Eight plan items addressed; all plausible indexed FamilySearch sources for this place and period were searched. Key gap: Texas death certificate not found; family not located post-1870; original 1870 census image not examined (index only). Ancestry-held Georgia records (pli_014) were not searched — this is the most significant remaining gap before advancing the tier.
- **Component 2 — Complete, accurate citations:** All cited; one source (src_004) supports all parentage assertions.
- **Component 3 — Analysis and correlation:** Two competing candidates identified and compared. The middle-initial distinction provides a meaningful differentiator. All facts (name, sex, birthplace, birth year) corroborate the identification of Martha J Wood in the Joseph B Wood household with LKYG-VKB.
- **Component 4 — Conflicting evidence:** Conflict c_003 (two competing candidates) resolved in favor of Joseph B Wood family based on middle-initial analysis. No other conflicting evidence found.
- **Component 5 — Soundly reasoned conclusion:** Probable. The conclusion rests on a single source (1870 census, derivative, indirect evidence for the parent-child relationship). The tier cannot reach Proved because: (a) only one source directly places Martha J Wood in the Wood household; (b) the original census image was not examined; (c) no independent corroborating source places Martha J Wood with Joseph B or Mary E Wood; (d) the family cannot be traced after 1870 to confirm the Texas migration trajectory.

## Conclusion

With a high probability, Martha J. Wood (LKYG-VKB) — mother of Jimmie Jewel Neal — was born approximately 1860 in Whitfield County, Georgia, as the daughter of Joseph B. Wood and Mary E. Wood. Both parents were Georgia-born and remained in Whitfield County at least through the 1870 census. The family had emigrated from Georgia by the time Martha married in Hill County, Texas in July 1879.

## Answer to Research Objective

The maternal grandparents of Jimmie Jewel Neal are, with high probability, **Joseph B. Wood** (born approximately 1836, Georgia) and **Mary E. Wood** (born approximately 1841, Georgia), both enumerated in Whitfield County, Georgia, in 1870.

## Next Steps to Advance the Tier

1. Examine the original 1870 census image (ark:/61903/1:2:M494-NX9) to confirm the transcription's accuracy and whether a relationship column or annotation is visible.
2. Search Ancestry's Georgia marriage records (Georgia Marriages 1699-1944, col. 7839; Georgia Compiled Marriages 1851-1900, col. 4453) for a marriage record for Joseph B. Wood and Mary E. Wood in Whitfield County.
3. Search Whitfield County, Georgia probate records (col. 1999178) for an estate or will of Joseph B. Wood naming Martha as a daughter.
4. Search Georgia tax digests (col. 4130006) for Joseph B. Wood in Whitfield County across the 1860s and 1870s to confirm annual residency.
5. Examine Martha's 1906 Hill County death certificate image if the full-image collection becomes accessible.

# Locality Guide: Hill County, Texas, 1850–1910

## Jurisdiction
Hill County was created in 1853 from Navarro County and has remained unchanged in its boundaries throughout the target period. County seat: Hillsboro. Standardized place: **Hill, Texas, United States**.

## Record Availability

### Marriage Records — EXCELLENT (Indexed + Images)
- **FamilySearch** holds fully digitized, 100% name-indexed Hill County marriage volumes covering 1873–1912 across multiple bound volumes (imageGroupNumbers 004820309, 004820310, 004820303–004820307, 004820616, 004820617).
- Also searchable via Texas, County Marriage Records, 1837–2010 (col. 1803985, 2.1M records) and Texas, County Marriage Index, 1837–1977 (col. 1803987).
- **Quirk:** Martha J. Wood married W.F. Lanham in 1869, then married James Monroe Neal in 1879 as 'Mattie Landham' (her widowed surname). Search both 'Wood' and 'Landham/Lanham' variants.

### Death Records — POST-1903 ONLY (Indexed + Images)
- Texas mandatory death registration began **1903**. No official death certificates exist for pre-1903 Hill County deaths.
- For 1903+: Texas, Deaths, 1890–1977 (col. 1983324, 4.5M records + images, indexed) and local Hill County death volumes (004820614, 100% indexed, 1903–1938).
- **Jimmie's 1884 birth has no birth certificate.** Martha J. Wood's 1906 death in Files Valley, Hill County should have a death certificate — search Texas Deaths 1890–1977.

### Birth Records — PRE-1903 ABSENT; DELAYED AFFIDAVITS EXIST
- No state birth certificates before 1903. For Jimmie Jewel Neal (born 10 July 1884), use:
  - **Delayed birth affidavits**: Hill County has massive delayed-birth volumes (imageGroupNumbers 008152748, 008507941, 008507942, 008507943, 008413381 — combined ~22,000+ images, full-text searchable, not name-indexed, covering 1867–1976). These frequently name parents and can establish pre-1903 births.
  - **1880 federal census** (highly indexed, national collection) — will show Jimmie in her parents' household.
  - Church baptismal records (limited coverage on FamilySearch for Hill County).
- Post-1903 birth registers for Hillsboro exist (008502334–008502336, 008992082) but are full-text searchable only (not name-indexed).

### Census Records

| 1890 | Partial survival (multi-county vol. 004679013) | 67% indexed |
| 1900 | Hill County | ~97% indexed (004118499, 004118498) |
| 1910 | National collection | Highly indexed |

### Tax Rolls
- Hill County tax rolls on FamilySearch: Reel 1 (1853–1878, 004616581), Reel 2 (1883–1887, 004616582), Reel 3 (1891, 004616583) — full-text searchable, not name-indexed.
- Texas, County Tax Rolls, 1837–1910 (col. 1827575, 4.6M records, indexed + images).

### Probate Records
- Texas, Probate Records, 1800–1990 (col. 2016287, 1.16M images) — **browse-only**, no indexing, no full-text. Access requires knowing approximate county and date.

### Church Records
- Blum, Hill County: Lutheran Parish Records 1886–1902 (imageGroupNumber 008984030, 439 images) — **browse-only**.
- Texas, Church Records, 1845–1957 (col. 2534484, 6374 images, browse-only) and 1852–1994 (col. 2790180, 6107 records + 2094 images).

### Deed Records
- Extensive digitized Hill County deed volumes (1881–1901+), all full-text searchable, 0% name-indexed. Search by name in full-text.

### Civil Court Records
- Hill County civil court cases 1872–1912 (multiple imageGroupNumbers 008689333–008689341), full-text searchable, not name-indexed.

### Other
- Texas, Voter Records, 1867–1918 (col. 3163398, 158K records, indexed).
- Texas, Civil War Confederate Service Records (col. 1932381, indexed).
- Hill County biography volume, 1892 (imageGroupNumber 007548348 series, browse-only).

# Georgia, United States — Locality Guide (1850–1880)

**For q_002: Parents of Martha J. Wood (born ~1859, Georgia)**

## Jurisdictional Context

Georgia has been a US state since 1776. All vital, probate, land, and court records were kept at the **county level**. Georgia had approximately 137 counties by 1860. Martha's specific county of birth is unknown; the 1860 and 1870 federal censuses are the primary locating tools.

**Critical gap**: Georgia had **no civil registration of births or deaths until 1919**. Birth and death facts for this period come from church records, census entries, delayed birth certificates, probate records, and tax digests.

## Key Collections on FamilySearch

- **County marriages** (col. 1927197, 1785–1950): 1.9M indexed records — primary marriage source.
- **Marriages** (col. 1674807, 1808–1967): 663K records, complementary.
- **Births/christenings** (col. 1674802, 1754–1960): Sparse 21K records; no civil registration pre-1919.
- **Church vital records** (col. 2790246, 1828–1991): 8K records; Methodist and Baptist common.
- **Probate records** (col. 1999178, 1742–1990): 203K indexed, 2.28M images; many browse-only.
- **Tax digests** (col. 4130006, 1787–1900): 2.88M records — annual census substitute by county.
- **Delayed birth/death records** (col. 3438747, 1829–1961): 99K records; often names parents.
- **Reconstruction oaths** (col. 2739725, 1867–1868): 182K records; adult white males.
- **Confederate pensions** (col. 3038333, 1861–1921): 154K records; can name family members.

## External Resources

- Ancestry: Georgia Marriage Records from Select Counties 1828–1978 (col. 4766), Georgia Marriages 1699–1944 (col. 7839), Compiled Marriages 1851–1900 (col. 4453), Select Births and Christenings 1754–1960 (col. 60264).
- Georgia Archives (georgiaarchives.org): Virtual Vault — colonial wills, death certificates, pension applications.
- Chronicling America / Georgia Historic Newspapers (dlg.usg.edu).

## Research Strategy for q_002

1. Martha's 1906 Hill County, Texas death certificate (Texas Deaths 1890–1977, col. 1983324) — highest priority; may name her parents directly. Already in loc_001 scope.
2. 1870 US census — Martha ~11 in Georgia; will appear in parents' household with family name and county.
3. 1860 US census — Martha ~1; appears as infant in parents' household.
4. Georgia County Marriages (col. 1927197) — check if Martha married Lanham in Georgia before moving to Texas.
5. Tax digests (col. 4130006) — once county identified, annual listings confirm Wood family's location.
6. Probate records (col. 1999178) — parent's will or estate may name Martha.

## Key Quirks

- No civil birth/death registration before 1919.
- County boundaries shifted frequently — verify for each census year.
- FamilySearch Wiki server was unavailable during this survey.
- 1890 census destroyed — use 1880 and 1900 with tax digests to bridge the gap.
- 'Wood' is a common surname; use age, location, and sibling/spouse names as disambiguation tools.
